title: Let scikit-learn fit it
prompt:
Finish `fit_line(hours, costs)` so it fits a `LinearRegression` and returns `(b, w)`: the bias and the weight. Remember that `X` needs one row per ticket, so turn each hour into a one-item list first.

Run it inside your virtual environment. `python3 fit.py` prints the line for the twelve fictional tickets.
hints: `X = [[h] for h in hours]` makes one row per ticket with one feature in each row.
`model = LinearRegression()` then `model.fit(X, costs)`. After fitting, `model.intercept_` is the bias and `model.coef_[0]` is the weight for the one feature.
explain_after: scikit-learn fits with `fit(X, y)`, where `X` has shape `(n_samples, n_features)` [ml-026]; your `X` has 12 rows of 1 feature. `LinearRegression` chooses the line with the smallest residual sum of squares [ml-032], the same score you computed by hand in *Score a guessed line*. The book's plain-Python recipe in `b04_byhand` lands on the same two numbers.
